rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Rental property owners and their agents may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator, meaning anyone operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function. Coordinators may not facilitate agreements that restrict competition. No person may engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination or perform a coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
rules.coverage_text: Rental property owners (persons owning, directly or indirectly, one or more rental residential dwelling units) and their agents, representatives or subcontractors; coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function; and any person engaging in parallel pricing coordination or performing a coordinating function. Residential dwelling units are any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended as a primary residence in the State.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Algorithmic devices exclude spreadsheets that operate without artificial intelligence and require human analysis, and databases that only use an algorithm to query unprocessed stored data. Coordinating functions exclude: use of competitively sensitive information solely for research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend lease terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices or collect competitively sensitive information for that purpose; and government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. Coordinators exclude government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls.
rules.penalty: Conduct is unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.). Sections 6 through 17 of that Act (C.56:9-6 through 9-17) apply to a violation of section 4. Complaints may be filed with the Attorney General.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
rules.interaction_text: A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act.  This subsection shall not be construed to prohibit the enactment of ordinances explicitly authorized or required by any other law.
